title: Amortized-Precision Quantization for Early-Exit Vision Transformers
claim: Perturbations from quantization destabilize dynamic exit decisions, so we model the risks and jointly optimize thresholds and bit-widths in a bi-level loop.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right separated by dashed lines; red dashed risk links, outer/inner loop boxes
description: Three panels split by dashed vertical lines. Left, 'Unstable Exit Decisions', has two line plots of confidence score across Layers 1-4 against a threshold line. The full-precision plot ends in a green 'Correct Exit' arrow. The quantized plot has a pink error band with red 'Premature Exit' and 'Delayed Exit' arrows. Middle, 'Modeling Risk', has two flowcharts. A blue full-precision stack (Layer 1-3, Final Result) sits beside a beige quantized stack (Q-Layer 1-3, Exit Gate, Exit Result). Red dashed connectors are labeled SQNR^-1, QID, BSR and PGR. Right, 'Bi-Level Optimization with APQ', has a blue outer-loop threshold box, a beige inner-loop bit-width box, a grey quantized early-exit ViT model with bit labels b1-b4 and exit gates, and a green self-distillation box. Black and red arrows link them in a cycle. The eye goes first to the left plots, then the red labels.
caption: Overview of MAQEE. Left: Quantization error perturbs early-exit decisions, causing either premature or delayed exits. Middle: Risk modeling for early exiting and quantization, including performance gap risk (PGR), boundary sensitivity risk (BSR), inverse SQNR, and quantization-induced drift (QID). Right: MAQEE solves Amortized-Precision Quantization (APQ) via bi-level optimization, where exit thresholds and layer-wise bit-widths are jointly optimized, with self-distillation for accuracy recovery.
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) achieve strong performance across vision tasks, yet their deployment with low-precision early exiting remains fragile. Existing quantization methods assume static full-depth execution, making them unstable when exit decisions are perturbed by quantization noise, which can amplify errors along dynamic inference paths. In this paper, we introduce Amortized-Precision Quantization (APQ), a utilization-aware formulation that accounts for layer utilization when modeling quantization error and reveals depth-precision trade-offs. Building on APQ, we propose Mutual Adaptive Quantization with Early Exiting (MAQEE), a bi-level framework that jointly optimizes exit thresholds and bit-widths under explicit risk control to improve inference stability. MAQEE establishes a superior Pareto frontier in the accuracy-efficiency trade-off across classification, detection, and segmentation, with comparisons at predefined task-specific performance targets. On ImageNet, it achieves 79.41% Top-1 accuracy while reducing BOPs by 10.9% relative to utilization-only allocation. Measurements of the deployed models on an RTX 5090 show GPU throughput improvements of $2.26\times$ on ImageNet and $3.06\times$ on CIFAR-100 over full-depth FP32 inference. Source code is available at https://github.com/Rui-Fang/MAQEE.
